patch_description:
The original implementation failed validation because it could lose row identity, mutate the effective column layout through merging, return an empty `column_orderings` list, rely on fragile tuple attribute access for column names, and create reordered frames whose rows could no longer be reliably mapped back to their original cells. It also optimized squared cell-length heuristics instead of the evaluator's serialized character-prefix objective.

This fix replaces the unsafe recursive dataframe mutation logic with bounded candidate construction. It preserves every input cell and row, supports mixed values and missing values, returns valid per-row column orderings, honors column merge/dependency ordering constraints, and selects among a small number of candidate orderings using the actual serialized Trie/LCP objective.
